rationale:
Evidence: the best result so far is iteration 4 (81.56), with five sensors at x = -0.06 to 0.06, y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.016, base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0.2, kd 1.2 and last_direction line loss. Iteration 5 scored 61.46 after changing three things at once: the sensor count (5 to 7), the forward row (y 0.07 to 0.08), and kd (1.2 to 1.5). The oval progress fell from 0.33 to 0.18, and the oval score fell from 135.7 to 76.4. Because these changes were confounded, I cannot tell which one caused the drop. The safest reading is that the 7-sensor, y = 0.08 layout is worse, so I revert to the iteration 4 geometry.

Across all 300 development trials, no run finished, and every run ended off track with max_error around 0.063 to 0.064 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. rms_error stays near 0.03 m. Oscillation was 0.15 to 0.19 in the best run, and the line was lost about once per run. The off-track limit cannot be raised by body width (it stays at 0.06 m), so the controller has to hold the robot tighter.

Change: restore the iteration 4 geometry exactly (5 sensors, x = -0.06 to 0.06, y = 0.07, size 0.016, same wheels and body). Keep base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5 and ki 0.2, since these produced the best score. Raise kd from 1.2 to 1.8 to damp the 0.15 to 0.19 steering jitter that drives the peak excursions. kd is the only controller value changed, so this race isolates it. Keep last_direction line loss and the same weights.

Expected result: lower steering oscillation and fewer line-loss events, with max_error nearer 0.06 and oval progress around 0.33 or higher. The score should land near 82 to 88, with a small chance of a first finish on the oval. The main risk is that kd of 1.8 amplifies sensor noise on the 16 mm footprints. If oscillation rises, the next revision should lower kd back toward 1.2 rather than change geometry.
